correctness.rationale: A face is present exactly when its complement contains a disconnected k-set. A k-set is connected precisely when successive gaps are at most two. For a complement of size k+1, deleting any interior point tests a two-step gap; every k-subset is connected exactly when the k+1 sites are consecutive. In a complement of size at least k+2, choose k+2 sorted sites and delete the second and third: the first gap is at least three, giving a disconnected k-set. This independently verifies both omitted layers. Top homology concentration is the cited squared-path shellability theorem. The augmented simplex differential is contraction by the sum of coordinates, so for the full (r-1)-skeleton the top cycles are the rth exterior power of its kernel (the reduced permutation representation over Q). Taking the signed Euler trace and removing each layer yields the claimed opposite signs; a fixed p-face has sign (-1)^floor(p/2). When r is odd there is exactly one omitted centered interval complement. For a connected symmetric k-set, the only options are paired sites meeting at the two positions nearest the center (even k), or the selected middle site with nearest left site at a or a-1 (odd n and odd k). Counting the admissible choices of size-two gaps gives B in each case. The known dimension and trace determine both multiplicities, even when both vanish. An independent 28-case check used graph reachability and reduced boundary matrices in the signed reversal eigenspaces modulo 101. It found no lower homology and recovered, in particular, (6,5), (12,13) and (31,36) for the three examples.
residual_risks: The modular calculation alone is not a claim about integral torsion or arbitrary characteristic. The general rational assertion follows from the analytic trace and shellability argument, not from finite checks.
